recommended_schedule: Push A - Pull A - Legs A - Push B - Pull B - Legs B - Rest
description: Organizes training by shared joint action so the triceps and delts are not re-fatigued the day after pressing. The six days are all distinct sessions: A days and B days rotate emphasis, so one rotation covers a full week at twice-weekly frequency per muscle.
best_for: Lifters with 1+ years of consistent training who can reliably get to the gym 5-6 days a week.

recommended_schedule: Chest+Back - Shoulders+Arms - Legs - Chest+Back - Shoulders+Arms - Legs - Rest
description: Pairs antagonist muscle groups in the same session, which allows supersetting and produces a large local pump. High per-session volume makes this the most recovery-demanding split here.
best_for: Advanced lifters with well-established work capacity and time for 80+ minute sessions.

recommended_schedule: Upper A - Lower A - Rest - Upper B - Lower B - Rest - Rest
description: Trains each half of the body twice weekly, with the A sessions biased toward heavy compound strength work and the B sessions toward higher-rep hypertrophy. The best evidence-supported ratio of results to time invested.
best_for: Almost everyone. The default recommendation for beginners through early-advanced lifters.

recommended_schedule: Anterior A - Posterior A - Rest - Anterior B - Posterior B - Rest - Rest
description: Divides the body by chain rather than by push/pull: quads, chest and front delts on anterior days, hamstrings, glutes, back and rear delts on posterior days. Concentrates hinge and pull fatigue into the same sessions, which protects the lower back.
best_for: Athletes and lifters who want structural balance, and anyone whose lower back gets beaten up by squatting and deadlifting in one session.

recommended_schedule: Full Body A - Rest - Full Body B - Rest - Full Body C - Rest - Rest
description: Every major movement pattern in every session, at three sessions per week. Highest frequency per muscle and the most forgiving structure if a session gets missed.
best_for: Beginners, anyone returning after a layoff, and time-constrained lifters training three days a week.

recommended_schedule: Push - Pull - Legs - Rest - Upper - Lower - Rest
description: Front-loads the week with a full push/pull/legs rotation, then adds an upper and a lower session to push each muscle group back toward twice-weekly frequency. Solves the main weakness of a 3-day PPL without demanding six training days.
best_for: Lifters who can train five days a week and want PPL's structure with better weekly frequency.

recommended_schedule: Push - Pull - Legs - Rest - Shoulders+Back - Rest - Rest
description: A four-day rotation with a dedicated fourth day for side delts, rear delts and lat width. Deliberately biased toward the muscles that create shoulder-to-waist taper rather than toward balanced whole-body development.
best_for: Lifters training for appearance rather than performance, who already have a base of general strength.
